# New renderings chosen in odyssey-101 (20.299–394)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀλεύομαι (20.300 ἀλεύατ’, 20.305 ἀλεύατο; the dodge of a thrown missile) | "avoided" | "avoided" | "dodged", "ducked" (too colloquial), "escaped" |
| σαρδάνιον μάλα τοῖον (20.301–302; meaning of σαρδάνιος unknown) | "bitterly, so very much so" | "a very bitter smile" (+ note: unknown; 'bitter, mocking' is the traditional guess) | "sardonically" (turns a word of unknown sense into the English word derived from it), "grimly", "scornfully" (each silently picks one guess) |
| ἔγχος ὀξυόεν (20.306, ἔγχεϊ ὀξυόεντι) | "a sharp spear" | "my sharp spear" | "pointed", "keen-edged" (an edge is not a point), "bronze-tipped" |
| ἀείκεια (20.308, ἀεικείας; cf. ἀεικής, ἀεικέα, ἀεικελίως) | "unseemliness" | "unseemly behaviour" | "outrage", "indecency", "abuse"; the family keeps "unseemly" throughout |
| ὅνδε δόμονδε (20.329; ὅνδε the accusative of ὅδε with δόμονδε) | "to this house" | "to this house" | "to his own house", "homeward" (drops ὅνδε) |
| νέμεσις (20.330) | "resentment" | "a cause for resentment" | "indignation", "blame", "retribution" (the divine Nemesis of later times) |
| ἰσχέμεναι (20.330, with μενέμεν; intransitive 'hold back') | "hold back" | "held back" / "held off" | "restrain themselves", "hold out" (each picks one reading of an object-less verb) |
| ὑπότροπος (20.332) | "returning" | "arrived back" | "turning back", "on his return journey" |
| ὀψὲ δὲ δὴ μετέειπε Δαμαστορίδης Ἀγέλαος (whole-line speech introduction, 20.321; late-speaker variant of the table's ὀψὲ δὲ δή … row) | "But late indeed spoke among them Damastor’s son, Agelaus:" | "At last Agelaus, son of Damastor, spoke among them:" | "answered" (nothing is being answered); "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε / προσέφη) |
| χεῖρας ἐφιέναι (20.386, χεῖρας ἐφήσει) | "lay his hands upon" | "lay hands on" | "raise his hand against", "set upon" (loses the hands) |
| ἀναιδέσι μνηστῆρσιν (20.386; dative, with μνηστῆρσιν) | "the shameless suitors" | "the shameless suitors" | "brazen", "impudent"; keeps the table’s ἀναιδής of persons "shameless" |
| καρτερὸς ἀνήρ (20.393, of Odysseus, after θεά) | "the strong man" | "a strong man" | "mighty" (reserved for ἴφθιμος / ὄβριμος), "stalwart", "powerful" |
| ἀχάριστος (20.392, ἀχαρίστερον) | "more graceless" | "more graceless" | "more unwelcome", "more joyless" (reserved for ἀτερπής), "more thankless" |
| γναθμοὶ ἀλλότριοι (20.347) | "others’ jaws" | "jaws that were not their own" | "strangers’ jaws", "foreign jaws"; the sense is that the laughter is not their own |
| αἱμοφόρυκτα κρέα (20.348; rare compound of αἷμα and φύρω) | "blood-smeared meat" | "meat smeared with blood" | "bloody", "dripping with blood" (fixes a degree the word may not carry), "blood-stained" |
| ἐπίμαστος (20.377; rare, from ἐπιμαίομαι; meaning uncertain) | "sought-out" | "sought-out" (+ note: meaning not known) | "begging", "much-sought", "picked up" (each silently picks one guess) |
| κακοξεινώτερος (20.376; disputed) | "worse-in-strangers" | "worse … where strangers are concerned" (+ note: 'worse at treating guests' or 'worse off in the guests he gets') | "more inhospitable", "unluckier in guests" (each silently picks one reading) |
| ἄχθος ἀρούρης (20.379) | "a burden of the plough-land" | "a burden on the plough-land" | "dead weight", "a useless burden on the earth"; ἄρουρα keeps the table’s "plough-land" |
| ἐς Σικελούς (20.383) | "to the Sicels" | "to the Sicels" | "to Sicily", "to the Sicilians" |
| κατ’ ἄντηστιν (20.387) | "right opposite" | "right opposite" | "facing the door", "at the threshold" (the Greek does not say what she faces) |
